cohort: 182 women with eclampsia carrying 34 weeks or more gestation
finding: Cesarean delivery, compared to planned vaginal delivery in women with eclampsia at or after 34 weeks of gestation, was associated with lower rates of severe maternal outcome, perinatal death, and improved perinatal outcomes, including Apgar scores at 5 minutes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was associated with better perinatal outcomes, including Apgar scores at 5 minutes and lower perinatal death rates, compared to vaginal delivery in women with eclampsia.
